title.narrative: Community-Focused Investments to Address Deforestation and Forest Degradation

description.narrative:
With assistance from the Forest Investment Program (FIP) under Climate Investment Funds (CIF), the project will provide a $17 million grant to the Government of Indonesia to address institutional, technical, and capacity-related barriers for REDD+ implementation in West Kalimantan, one of the top five provinces contributing to GHG emissions with a mean deforestation rate of 132,500 ha per year.
The project forms a part of Indonesia''s forest investment plan and will complement projects by the World Bank and International Finance Corporation (IFC). The project will promote inclusive growth and environmental sustainability by investing in community-focused REDD+ activities (e.g., community-based land use planning, community-led forest monitoring and forest fire management, community-assisted forest regeneration and maintenance, community-based eco-tourism) in selected districts and/or forest management units (FMUs) to address deforestation drivers such as illegal logging, forest conversion to agriculture, and uncontrolled fires. The project will strengthen capacity of district and provincial governments in West Kalimantan, provide policy support to harmonize sub-national policies for carbon stock enhancement with national policies, and establish non-monetary incentives, safeguard systems and equitable and gender-responsive benefit sharing arrangements
The project will build on lessons from other REDD+ initiatives by the government and development partners such as Norway, Australia, Germany, Japan, and USA, and establish a sound base for performance-based REDD+ payments. By promoting sustainable forest management, the project will not only reduce GHG emissions and enhance carbon stocks but also provide livelihood co-benefits such as poverty reduction, improved quality of life for forest communities, protection of indigenous peoples' tenure rights, and enhanced conservation of biodiversity and ecosystem services.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Community-focused and gender-responsive REDD+ pilot projects in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang districts implemented. Indicator: 1,880 ha of deforested land brought under improved community-based agroforestry systems. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The Project has completed the community based agroforestry program (1,880 Ha) in 2021. In 2022, the Project completed the last monitoring on agroforestry in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang.
BPSKL is the main Implementing Unit for agroforestry, in cooperation with Forest Management Units. Through a total of 108 community groups were established and involved 1.938 people (1.156 men and 782 women). FMU, supported by PISU, completed all technical design document through a participative approach. Series of consultations have been conducted to identify land for the program, establishment of farmer groups, and selection of forest and agriculture plant species.
From the monitoring of agroforestry plant in 2022, the average of plant survival rate is above 75%. DG PSKL has developed a guideline for agroforestry monitoring and will be a new standard for PSKL to implement agroforestry program in the future (Decree of the Directorate of Social Forestry and Environmental Partnership No.: SK.19/PSKL/PUPS/PSL. 2/7/2022 concerning Monitoring and Evaluation for Agroforestry Implementation). Data Source: PPMS reports, FMU management plans, FIP progress report

Output: Community-focused and gender-responsive REDD+ pilot projects in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang districts implemented. Indicator: 17,000 ha of natural forestland brought under community-based forest management. Achievement: 16154 Progress/Status: The achievement of the CBFM activities has exceeded the target.
Until December 2021, the project has achieved a total of 27,196 hectares from the total target of 17,000 hectares. These total area covers 8 Village Forest Agreement in Sintang (5 villages) and Kapuas Hulu (1 village) and three Conservation Partnership Agreement in Vega, Pulau Majang and Tanjung Lasa. Additionally, the Project also facilitated 5 Social Forestry agreement (4 village forest and one customary forest).
Dir PUPS and BPSKL has also facilitated the development of Social Forestry Management Plan and Business Plan. Facilitation with the potential investor on voluntary forest carbon has also been implemented in the Q3-Q4 2022 by the local NGO PRCF. The facilitation includes development of baseline data and PES Concept Note in Kapuas Hulu (Tanjung Lasa, Batu Lintang) and Sintang (Kayu Dujung and Radin Jaya) Data Source: PPMS reports, FMU management plans, FIP progress report

Output: Community-focused and gender-responsive REDD+ pilot projects in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang districts implemented. Indicator: 500 community members trained in implementing community-based REDD+ pilot projects Achievement: 142 Progress/Status: The achievement of the Training activities for Community related Implementing Community Based REDD+ has exceeded the target.
Training on REDD+ were conducted for West Kalimantan REDD+ working groups and FMU staff (461 staff), and the community members as the project beneficiaries (3917 community members, of which 1243 are women). Data Source: Training reports, PPMS reports

Output: Community-focused and gender-responsive REDD+ pilot projects in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang districts implemented. Indicator: 6,000 ha of degraded land rehabilitated through community-based assisted natural regeneration. Achievement: 1500 Progress/Status: All 6000 Ha of the ANR target have been achieved (100%).
ANR guidelines has been established through the Decree of Directorate General of Sustainable Production Management SK.10/PHPL/SET/KUM. 1/1/2020 concerning Implementation of Assisted Natural Regeneration. Technical design for ANR has also been completed and was divided into three Implementing Units, i.e., TNBKDS (2,000 Ha), BPHL (1,500 Ha), and BPSKL (2,500 Ha). The implementation of 6,000 Ha ANR has involved a total of 18 community groups with total members of 480 people (393 men and 87 women).
The ANR groups has also received training on the utilization of non-timber forest product (e.g., rattan, fish, honey, food product). As part of the Social Forestry agreement area, ANR group also received further facilitation for a voluntary forest carbon project funded by NGOs (PRCF, AMAN and SAMPAN) using the CCB (conservation, community and biodiversity) and other schemes. Data Source: PPMS reports, FMU management plans, FIP progress report

Output: Community-focused and gender-responsive REDD+ pilot projects in Kapuas Hulu and Sintang districts implemented. Indicator: Four FMUs in two districts implement REDD+ pilot projects in a participatory manner. Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All four Long-term forest management plans (RPHJPs) of Unit X, North Sintang, Unit XXI, South Kapuas Hulu, TNBKDS and North Kapuas Hulue were approved.
By December 2022, REDD+ pilot projects have been implemented in all four FMUs. All project activities have been synchronized with the long term forest management plan at three FMUs and the Betung Kerihun Danau Sentarum National Park Management Plan (such as land based program of agroforestry, assisted natural regeneration, and ecosystem restoration program; community/livelihood empowerment program; and capacity building program). FMU staffs have received training related to carbon accounting, forest monitoring program, forest inventory and sustainable forest management. The FIP-1 Project facilitated registration of REDD+ project into the National Registry System (SRN) by FMUs in 2019 and was updated in 2021. The Project also provided all necessary data to the sub-national REDD+ Working Group to be inputted into the Safeguard Information System for REDD+ (September 2022). Additionally, from the 17 villages, 15 villages have been registered to the national Village Climate Program (PROKLIM). Data Source: PPMS reports, FMU management plans, FIP progress report

Until December 2022, guidelines on GRM are prepared (in 2019) and operationalized (2019-now). It also has been discussed with relevant stakeholders in Sintang, Kapuas Hulu and Pontianak. Poster and brochures for GRM are disseminated to stakeholders in Kapuas Hulu, Sintang and Pontianak. FIP-1 has also involved in the establishment of a Joint Secretariat of REDD+ in Sintang, where Conflict Resolution is one of the working group. Results from FIP-1 on GRM and tenurial has also used by POKJA REDD+ West Kalimantan in developing the Emission Reduction Intervention Strategy document. Data Source: Provincial reports. Output: Subnational fiscal policies on REDD+ harmonized with national policies. Indicator: At least three gender-responsive proposals for mobilizing subnational REDD+ funding developed. Achievement: 12 Progress/Status: The Project has exceeded the target. A total of 12 proposals were facilitated or prepared by the Project for potential fund mobilization. Although none of the proposals were accepted for FIP dedicated grant mechanism, the project has continued facilitation of four villages in Kapuas Hulu to enter the cooperation with the Lestari Capital as the forest carbon project developer.
The summary of proposals submitted to various organizations are listed below: 1. 8 proposals submitted to DGM (dedicated grant mechanism) through Samdhana Institute. None of them were succesful due to the different scope expected from DGM and the targeted villages of FIP-1 Project; 2. A proposal for remote sensing supported by ESA (European Space Agency) was submitted and was successful. The Project supports the National Park in land cover mapping within the national park boundary. The project is ongoing (internal assessment by the team). A training will be conducted for the TNBKDS in 2023; 3. Various proposal preparation support to the West Kalimantan REDD+ Working Group (GCF REDD+ readiness program). Currently, the Feasibility Study is being conducted, in collaboration with GIZ FORCLIME project. One part of the scope is to strengthen the REDD+ institution, and another scope will include Kapuas Hulu and Sintang for REDD+ planning and implementation (2024-2030); 4. Development of proposals for voluntary carbon scheme (Community, Climate and Biodiversity). 5 villages in Kapuas Hulu and 2 villages in Sintang are proposed to receive facilitation from Rimba Collective program by Lestari Capital. Data Source: PPMS reports, MOEF reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not available Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not available Target year: 2023 Target value: 3 Actual value: 12

Output: Subnational fiscal policies on REDD+ harmonized with national policies. Indicator: At least three subnational policies (fiscal, benefit sharing, and incentive mechanisms) harmonized with national policies. Achievement: 3 Progress/Status: The Project has achieved the target and has supported three sub national policies related to fiscal, benefit sharing, an incentive mechanism.
FIP-1 have been involved in three regulations: 1. Two drafts of Governor regulations on BSM and Environmental Fund Flow. The draft has not been continued due to level of priority, but the Project has developed a Guidelines on BSM that can be used by the Provincial government for future REDD+ program; 2. Regulation on Non-Timber Forest Product Management (incentive for private sectors and village entities). The regulation has been harmonized with the central government at the Ministry of Law. This regulation has been issued (Governor regulation No. 33/2022); and 3. Support in the revision of the Regional Regulation No. 8/2021 concerning the Management and Protection of Mangrove and Peatland. The revision was completed and the regulation has been harmonized with the central government at the Ministry of Law Data Source: PPMS reports, MOEF reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not available Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not available Target year: 2023 Target value: 3 Actual value: 3
